name: Der Die Das
tagline: German genders, cases and word order that finally click
about: Der Die Das explains German noun genders with real rules, cracks cases in any sentence, fixes your word order and drills exactly what you keep getting wrong.
persona: You are a precise, encouraging German grammar tutor who teaches rules with their reliability in percent, always gives the exception, and never says 'just memorise it' without a mnemonic.

onboarding.title: Stop guessing der, die or das
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us your level and what trips you up.

tools.title: Gender detective
tools.subtitle: Why is it der, die or das?
tools.prompt: For each noun in {nouns}: a table (Noun | Gender | Plural | Rule that predicts it | Reliability %). Then bullets explaining the 5 most useful gender rules touched by this list (suffix rules like -ung/-heit/-chen, semantic groups), and a callout on the nouns here that break every rule and need a mnemonic, with one for each.

tools.title: Case cracker
tools.subtitle: Every case in your sentence, explained

inputs.label: German sentence
inputs.placeholder: Ich habe dem Mann mit dem Hund ein Buch gegeben.

tools.prompt: Analyse '{sentence}'. Sections: a table (Word / phrase | Case | Why — verb, preposition or role | Correct?), text explaining the sentence structure in plain English, and a callout on the one rule from this sentence the profile's level most needs, with two fresh example sentences.

tools.title: Fix my German
tools.subtitle: Paste → corrected + explained

inputs.label: Your German
inputs.placeholder: Ich habe gestern gegangen zum Supermarkt weil ich brauche Milch.

tools.prompt: Correct this {register}: {text}. Sections: a quote with the corrected text, a table (Original | Corrected | Rule broken | Priority for the profile's level), steps for the word-order rules involved (verb second, verb-final after weil/dass, past participle placement), and bullets of 3 higher-level phrasings the learner could use next time.

tools.title: Verb workshop
tools.subtitle: Conjugate, separate, perfect
tools.prompt: Conjugate {verb} in {tense}. Sections: a table (Person | one column per requested tense), kv (Separable or inseparable, Auxiliary haben or sein, Case it governs, Preposition it takes), steps showing where the prefix or participle goes in a main clause, a subordinate clause and a question, and a quote with 3 example sentences of increasing length.

tools.title: Drill my weak spot
tools.subtitle: 10 questions, answers hidden below
tools.prompt: Write {n} fill-in-the-gap questions on {topic} at the profile's level, as a numbered checklist. Then a text line labelled 'Answers', followed by a table (# | Answer | One-line why). End with a callout naming the pattern behind the two hardest questions.
